meta.description: Common NCERT Ch 7 How do Organisms Reproduce? misconceptions

asexual_sexual_swap.feedback: Asexual reproduction uses one parent with no gamete fusion; sexual reproduction involves two parents and fusion of male and female gametes.
asexual_sexual_swap.calm_prompt: One parent or two? Gametes involved or not?

pollination_fertilisation_swap.feedback: Pollination is transfer of pollen to stigma; fertilisation is fusion of male and female gametes inside the ovule.
pollination_fertilisation_swap.calm_prompt: Pollen reaching stigma, or gametes fusing?

male_female_organ_swap.feedback: Vas deferens, testes, and epididymis are male reproductive parts; ovary, uterus, and fallopian tube are female parts.
male_female_organ_swap.calm_prompt: Trace the organ — sperm path or egg path?

binary_budding_swap.feedback: Binary fission splits one cell into two equal parts (Amoeba); budding produces a small outgrowth that separates (yeast, Hydra).

dna_copying_confusion.feedback: DNA copying during reproduction ensures the offspring gets a complete set of genetic instructions; variations arise from slight inaccuracies in copying.
dna_copying_confusion.calm_prompt: Why must DNA be copied faithfully before cell division?
